extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of philosophy (metaphysics, philosophy of mind), Bergson scholars, general educated readers interested in theory of knowledge
extracted.subtask_description: Expository/philosophical chapter arguing a method for metaphysics and theory of knowledge focused on duration, consciousness, and the relation between intellect and matter. It prescribes how philosophy should approach life, science, and the engendering of concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish the inert from the living
rubrics_metrics.description: Trace a line of demarcation between the inert and the living; treat the living with a special attitude distinct from that applied to inert matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The living only fits intellectual frames artificially; positive science is at home with unorganized/inert matter but treats life by applying the same mechanistic forms, producing a symbolic and relative knowledge. Philosophy must examine the living without reservation and with 'other eyes than those of positive science.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not deduce categories a priori; engender them
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid compressing intellect into an a priori principle and then deducing categories of thought from it; instead, trace the genesis (origins) of the categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metaphysical systems that take the intellect as given (condensed or expanded) may define intellect but cannot show its genesis. Philosophy should seek to engender the categories by a method that goes beyond mere analytical deduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy must not leave all facts to positive science
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject the division of labor that confines facts to science and principles to philosophy, because that hands philosophy a ready-made, unconscious metaphysic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the philosopher accepts scientific descriptions uncritically, he merely formulates more precisely the metaphysic implicit in science (a registration court). Philosophy must intervene actively in questions of fact to avoid importing unexamined intellectual frames.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the postulate of an a priori abstract unity of nature/intellect
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not assume in advance that nature is one and that the function of intellect is to embrace it in its entirety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepting this postulate yields either metaphysical dogmatism or skepticism and exaggerates confidence in the individual mind; philosophy should be modest, collective, and progressive rather than a single unitary vision taken 'to be accepted or left.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use action/experience to break the circle of reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that purely reflective reasoning cannot extend intelligence beyond itself; practical action and lived experience can create new faculties and break the vicious circle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogy of learning to swim: one cannot deduce swimming purely by reasoning about walking; one must act (enter the water). Similarly, to extend intelligence one must thrust it outside itself by will and action rather than solely by speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy's method: speculative 'seeing' (intuition) rather than instrumental science
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy should speculate—to see—rather than adopt the instrumental, action-oriented stance of positive science when studying life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where science treats objects in terms of how they can be acted upon (instruments), philosophy should free itself from those forms and 'see' the living in its own terms to achieve metaphysical knowledge that complements scientific truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentrate on pure duration to reconstruct genesis of intellect
rubrics_metrics.description: Return attention to immediate experience—pure duration—where past swells into a continually new present, as the point where the intellect's origin can be grasped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By intensifying self-consciousness and tracing the regression of extra-spatial into spatial, philosophy can follow how duration degrades into extension and thereby 'engender' the categories rather than assume them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize degrees of spatiality and avoid treating space as absolute
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that spatiality admits of degrees; do not treat the notion of space as a ready-made a priori form wholly separate from temporal/durational processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kant's argument that space is an a priori form is critiqued: the mind sketches a movement toward spatiality and matter only attains spatiality progressively. Philosophical method must account for intermediate degrees rather than assume perfect spatiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consciousness overflows the intellect; treat conscious states as indivisible and new
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept that states of consciousness are indivisible, novel, and incommensurable with intellect—intellect reconstitutes them only after the fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The intellect grasps states by taking externalized views and reconstructing them, but the lived state itself 'overflows' the intellect; analytic methods risk losing what is essential about duration and lived experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit science to its proper domain (inert matter); beware of overextension
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat positive science as properly directed to inert matter; extending scientific conceptual frames deeper into life makes its knowledge increasingly symbolic, provisional, and conventional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Science's mathematical precision is apt for inert matter because action uses inert instruments; when applied to life, the scientific model becomes relative to practical contingencies and must be supplemented by metaphysical insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt the fourth alternative to Kant: progressive adaptation of intellect and matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject the three Kantian alternatives (mind determined by things, things by mind, or pre-established harmony) in favor of an account where intellect and matter progressively adapt to one another to attain a common form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This adaptation is the 'inversion of the same movement' creating both intellectuality of mind and materiality of things; it grounds a view where knowledge of matter is approximative but not merely relative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent philosophy sliding into either metaphysical dogmatism or skepticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid adopting the mechanistic unity of science as metaphysical absolute (which leads to dogmatism) or universal relativism (which leads to skepticism); pursue a philosophy that can be completed progressively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If philosophy cedes empirical fact entirely to science, it forfeits its role and ends up either hypostasizing a vacuous unity or denying knowledge's value. The correct path is collective, progressive inquiry that expands human understanding without presuming finality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy should remount physics' incline—construct a reversed psychology/cosmology
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of following physics further into spatialization, metaphysics should retrace the incline and bring matter back to its origins, building a cosmology that is a reversed psychology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: What appears positive to the physicist is an interruption or inversion of the true positivity; metaphysics must restore origins in psychological terms by following the regression from spatiality back into duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not accept scientific results uncritically as final truth about life
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that scientific descriptions of living phenomena are shaped by practical needs and intellectual habits and therefore require philosophical revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific problem-solving is provisional and depends on the order problems are posed; thus scientific theories are conventional 'of fact' and must be corrected by philosophical insight when applied to life.
